metadataReview.note: Reviewed Gregorian date: 2 November 1642. The HAB/Freiburg edition explicitly pairs 23 October/2 November for the second Breitenfeld battle. The imported 23 October is Old Style even though the cached P585 labels it Gregorian; the correction follows the historical edition rather than silently trusting that erroneous calendar tag. The former Leipzig-centre coordinate is withdrawn after a separate geographical review. The official Westsachsen landscape framework maps the second Breitenfeld battlefield north of Leipzig (map 2.6-39), and the Saxon State Archives independently locates the 1642 battle at Breitenfeld. These sources do not supply an exact replacement point. The event remains available without a map point; the 1631 battlefield monument and the later capture of Leipzig are not substituted for the 1642 field.

note:
Reviewed CDB90 match 12, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: Approve the exact whole battle after the separately proposed correction to 2 November 1642 Gregorian. The HAB/Freiburg scholarly diary introduction explicitly equates 23 October with 2 November and identifies Torstensson against Leopold Wilhelm and Piccolomini’s imperial-Saxon army. CDB90 IMP ARMY and SW ARMY are retained as two aggregate commands; no additional Saxon total is added. Both personnel strengths are initial-strength estimates, with no source reinforcements. The institutional evidence establishes chronology and force identity, not exact confirmation of the CDB90 30000/25000 strengths or 15000/5000 casualty estimates. Identity review (attacker; original CDB90 name SW ARMY): The HAB/Freiburg introduction identifies the Swedish field command at the second Breitenfeld battle. Original SW ARMY retained in each CDB90 qualifier. Identity review (defender; original CDB90 name IMP ARMY): The scholarly introduction explicitly identifies the imperial-Saxon command under Leopold Wilhelm and Piccolomini. This is the aggregate IMP ARMY record, not separately quantified coalition members. Historical published participant Q12548 is replaced by this event-local aggregate; its exact original item and P710 statement citations are preserved here as provenance. It is not an additional separately scaled component.
